background: The [Parity RPC trait at 55c90d4](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L28-L70) exposes nine distinct methods. They did not arrive as one indivisible feature: [multi-call was added in 2017](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/f157461ee19740c8d013bb9885d3aa0aa5f91a8a) and [block replay in 2018](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/df5d27d5163e8d6f6d00f4f8996ce384fcf804cf). The [OpenEthereum trace guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module) also distinguishes ad hoc execution from indexed historical filtering, which requires tracing to have been enabled. This history supports specifying method contracts separately; it does not establish that every modern client must implement every method.

The [2026 standardization issue](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890) records that Erigon, Reth and Nethermind expose the nine-method namespace, while Besu lacks individual replay and Geth has a different debug tracing API. The [draft PR](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/895) leaves method scope and support policy for review. An unimplemented method must remain distinguishable from an implemented lookup that found no records; whether the profile is optional or split between execution and historical search is still a policy decision, not client agreement.

[Besu #6597](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/6597) requested `trace_replayTransaction` for Blockscout. A Besu contributor said the core team did not plan to implement it because it is outside the Ethereum specification and suggested `debug_traceTransaction`; another user noted that exposing the `DEBUG` namespace on a public endpoint was undesirable. The issue was closed due to age in March 2025, without an implementing PR. This records the team's stated scope at that time, not a current agreement on this profile.

[Besu #11357](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/11357), opened 2026-09-23, asks the team to reconsider individual replay using this project's cross-client H01 evidence, or to state that core support remains out of scope. [Besu #9699](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/9699) separately tracks pre-execution state changes that transaction replay must account for. Neither issue changes the behavior observed in the pinned builds.
items.next_step: Agree the optional-method/conformance model with client teams; no assumption of adopted optional status or Geth support.
items.rationale: A caller should be able to distinguish an unsupported operation from a valid query with no trace.
items.recommendation: Specify each method independently; make the implemented subset discoverable or explicitly declared. An unsupported method should return -32601, never a fabricated empty result. Add individual replay to Besu when practical rather than removing it from the common API.
items.title: Method coverage

background: Parity modeled `trace_get` as a [single `Vec<Index>` path returning an optional object](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L84-L93). Its [trace database compares the full path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L267-L286), so an empty path identifies the root rather than a flat position. Parity [fixed `traceAddress` handling in 2016](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/948b614f4072d89678810c34b5ae23a1eb7bdf00). Its [Index deserializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/index.rs#L23-L64) accepted hex and decimal strings, but not JSON number tokens.

The pinned [Erigon lookup](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L134-L149) also compares the whole path; [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L220-L242) uses the first supplied index as a flat position; [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L402-L424) returns a collection. The path and singular-result proposal follows Parity, but changing either client needs compatibility review.

Parity's [localized-trace serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L501-L535) writes `traceAddress` from `Vec<usize>` as JSON integers. The draft retains that output representation and uses hex quantities for request indices. The conversion belongs at the caller boundary, not in trace responses. Requiring minimal hex input deliberately narrows Parity's acceptance of decimal strings; tree-path meaning does not depend on the two directions having identical wire types.
items.next_step: Choose the tree-path contract and align Reth/Nethermind; the positive nested discriminator is now available.
items.rationale: The lookup argument should identify the same path that traceAddress describes, with a singular result matching the method name.
items.recommendation: Treat the argument as one traceAddress path: [] is root, ["0x0"] first child, ["0x6","0x0"] a nested child. Return one trace object or null for a missing transaction/path. Keep output traceAddress entries as JSON integers; callers convert them to minimal hex quantities for trace_get input. Integer request entries return -32602.
items.title: trace_get selector and return shape

background: Parity's [original matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L42-L111) treats each address list as alternatives, combines sender and recipient with `&&`, and builds the Cartesian product of address blooms for indexed search. An empty list matches all addresses. The [RPC filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L28-L68) had no `mode` field and rejected unknown fields. Thus intersection follows the Parity implementation, while explicit union is a later Erigon compatibility extension, not an original namespace option.

In [Erigon #2119](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/2119), banteg asked in June 2021 for an intersection option to narrow calls from a sender set to a recipient set. Erigon merged the [mode implementation in #3167](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3167) in January 2022, corrected the list-level boolean composition in [#3304](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3304), and [backported it to stable in #3305](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3305). This is established client precedent for retaining an explicit mode.

[Alloy #4216](https://github.com/alloy-rs/alloy/pull/4216), merged on 2026-09-22, cites H03 and changes the default from union to intersection while retaining explicit union. Its tests cover OR within each list, AND between lists, empty lists, and both recognized modes. Reth uses [Alloy's matcher](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L354-L371), but the tested Reth builds and [main@47c2166bc4](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/47c2166bc48bba25b95787c1f0640ec42bb9dee0/Cargo.lock) (checked 2026-09-23) still lock Alloy 2.4.2, which predates the PR. Reth needs dependency uptake and a retest before its observed result changes.

The pinned draft accepts recognized modes. The mode cases were recaptured on 2026-09-23 against every tested build, including one-sided `union` queries. The Geth draft fork adopted recognized modes and nullable address lists at [40eecf3647](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/commit/40eecf3647f26546df9dbf72ce48f372df469ef2). Reth's null-list rejections are tracked under [H04](H04.md).
items.next_step: Confirm the default and the two recognized modes with client teams. Retest Reth after it picks up Alloy #4216.
items.rationale: Adding a second filter should narrow a search. This matches `eth_getLogs`, where each topic position accepts a list of alternatives (OR) and all positions must match (AND); a null position is a wildcard, just as an omitted or empty address list is here. Explicit union is still useful when callers need one globally paginated result across both address sets.
items.recommendation: Use OR within each address list and AND between `fromAddress` and `toAddress` by default. An omitted, null, or empty side imposes no restriction. Accept optional `mode: "intersection"` (the default) and `mode: "union"` (match either populated side); reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.
items.title: Filter composition and mode

background: Parity's [RPC filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L28-L67) made both address arrays optional and converted an omitted or JSON-null field to an empty vector. Its [address matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L28-L63) explicitly treats that vector as matching all addresses; the bloom path gives it an unrestricted bloom rather than a zero-match search. This is an inherited API convention, not merely an intuition about empty filters.

The modern clients differ at both input decoding and matching. The pinned [Nethermind matcher](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TxTraceFilter.cs#L56) and [Erigon filter](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L311) must be read together with the linked empty/null cases: accepting a JSON field does not prove it is treated as unrestricted. H03 determines how nonempty sides compose; this decision only establishes when a side has no constraint.
items.next_step: Review the compatibility choice to accept null alongside omitted and empty lists; retain separate checks for special-action membership.
items.rationale: Programmatically adding an empty optional filter should not erase all results.
items.recommendation: Treat an omitted, null or empty address list as no restriction. A nonempty list restricts that side. Compare address bytes independently of hex letter case.
items.title: Empty address lists

background: Parity [added reward traces in 2017](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/06862c7dee400e3b9f37c6cfdae52c081ee9d7f1) for consensus payouts and then [made transaction IDs optional](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/1f3f91136ca9438336e5eb824ce31555ac116fae) because a reward is not a transaction. Its [serializer test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L814-L831) expects a `reward` action with null transaction localization. This explains why the trace model has non-transaction records at all.

[EIP-3675](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#block-and-ommer-rewards) removed the PoW block and ommer balance increases at the Merge while leaving transaction fees in place. [EIP-4895](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4895) later introduced withdrawals as block-level balance changes, but neither Parity's reward encoding nor that EIP defines a `trace_*` withdrawal action. The observed Besu and Nethermind zero-value reward placeholders therefore should not be treated as actual post-Merge rewards; whether to include withdrawals or other system changes needs an explicit separate trace contract.
items.next_step: Specify which protocol operations belong in this namespace. Keep withdrawals and system transitions separate from transaction call traces unless explicitly included.
items.rationale: A reward trace should correspond to a real protocol operation, not a zero-value placeholder that changes pagination.
items.recommendation: Do not emit a synthetic PoW block reward on a PoS block. Represent real protocol balance changes only under explicitly defined semantics; keep transaction tips in transaction accounting. Define nullable localization fields separately for non-transaction records.
items.title: Post-merge reward records

background: Parity's [trace lookup methods](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L2052-L2110) returned `Option`: absent transaction, missing trace data and disabled tracing could all become JSON `null`; [mocked RPC tests](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/tests/mocked/traces.rs#L83-L166) confirm null for missing trace storage. By contrast, its [ad hoc call path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L108-L127) raises an explicit state-pruned error when required state is absent. Separating absence from unavailability improves on a real historical ambiguity.

[EIP-1474](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#error-codes) names `-32001` Resource not found and `-32002` Resource unavailable. [execution-apis #636](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/636), merged on 2025-10-14, defines `4444` (Pruned history unavailable) for several eth/debug methods, including `eth_getLogs`. Extending that code to trace methods and pruned execution state is the proposal here, not an already adopted trace policy. A requested range must not silently become a partial search at the retention boundary. [Reth #27367](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27367) and the linked pruning cases show why unavailable state must not serialize as an apparent empty result.

[EIP-4444's JSON-RPC discussion](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4444#json-rpc-changes) notes that pruned indexing may prevent distinguishing an unknown hash from an old one. When this prevents establishing absence, return unavailable history rather than claiming `null` proves the transaction never existed. An absent path in a successfully obtained tree still returns `null`. Harmonizing missing individual replay to `null` is also deliberate: Parity's replay path used a transaction-not-found error, unlike its indexed lookups.
items.next_step: Choose an unavailable-history error contract. Extend the retention fixture to Erigon, Nethermind and Besu; the current pruning result is Reth-only.
items.rationale: Not found, empty, unsupported and unavailable are different states that callers need to distinguish.
items.recommendation: Return null for a well-formed lookup of an unknown transaction or trace path, consistently across these methods. Reserve [] for a successfully evaluated collection with no elements. Preserve -32601 for unsupported methods and use errors for unavailable/pruned state instead of pretending data is absent. Unknown selected blocks and range endpoints return -32001 (Resource not found), separately from 4444 for pruned required state. If pruned indexing prevents establishing whether a hash is absent, return 4444 rather than a definitive not-found result.
items.title: Missing transactions and paths

background: [Parity issue #8725](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/issues/8725) reported that `trace_replayBlockTransactions` returned per-transaction state diffs without hashes, forcing callers to pair array positions with block transactions. [The 2018 fix](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/526c61e2c053f7ef98be93b118120ab585f4aaad) added a distinct `TraceResultsWithTransactionHash` type for block replay. The [Parity RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L59-L70) and [response structs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L671) retained a plain `TraceResults` for individual replay, whose request already supplies the hash.

The [OpenEthereum examples](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module) include `transactionHash` in block-replay items but omit it in individual replay, as does the pinned [Reth implementation](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs). Requiring it in both is an intentional additive contract improvement: each replay result remains identifiable when cached, forwarded or detached from the request. The benefit is consistent self-contained envelopes, not restoration of the original individual-replay shape. Clients and strict decoders need compatibility review.
items.next_step: Confirm the envelope schema and add one serialization test; treat missing support in Besu separately under H01.
items.rationale: A replay object should keep its identity when stored or moved out of its original request context.
items.recommendation: Include transactionHash in both individual and per-transaction block-replay envelopes. Do not require it for unsigned trace_call or trace_callMany simulations.
items.title: Replay transactionHash field

background: Parity's [trace-option mapping](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L36-L42) toggles transaction, VM and state tracers independently. Its [common response type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L646) always carries execution `output` and a trace vector, while VM and state components are optional. The [OpenEthereum `trace_call` example](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_call) shows empty bytes as `0x` and unrequested components as `null`; Parity's [mocked RPC test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/tests/mocked/traces.rs#L169-L177) confirms the stable envelope with an empty trace array.

The pinned [Erigon response type](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L81-L88) permits a nil trace slice, which serializes as `null` unless initialized. Nethermind's [replay writer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/ParityReplayEnvelopeWriter.cs#L14-L58) writes `output` from the trace object independently of the selected details; the observed stateDiff-only loss therefore needs tracing/data-flow investigation, not a different response schema.
items.next_step: Preserve the execution return bytes independently of which optional trace components are requested.
items.rationale: Empty bytes and an unavailable value are different, and selecting an auxiliary view should not change the primary call result.
items.recommendation: Keep a stable envelope: output is the execution return bytes ("0x" when empty); trace is [] when not requested; stateDiff and vmTrace are null when not requested. Requesting a different tracer must not change or erase the returned execution output.
items.title: Empty output and unrequested components

background: Parity [added explicit trace errors in 2016](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/da2c2e5fc67010dbd6e6300d856b0dfa06f0b569). Its [failure enum](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/error.rs#L24-L95) maps VM failures to stable labels including Reverted and Out of gas; its [trace serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L501-L536) emits an `error` field on failure and omits `result`. Parity's [failure serialization test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L722-L743) locks this shape. The pinned [Nethermind writer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/ParityReplayEnvelopeWriter.cs#L94-L105) follows the same error-versus-result branch.

[EIP-140](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-140#specification) requires REVERT to retain returndata and unused gas for the caller, unlike an exceptional out-of-gas halt. That execution fact motivates preserving observed revert bytes and measured gas where a trace format can express them, but it does not itself define a failed-frame JSON `result`. The Besu and Nethermind cases should be separated into missing failure status, missing execution data, and wire-shape choices.

The draft deliberately requires an explicit failed result, populated with available execution data or null, rather than preserving Parity’s error-only shape. This makes failure data discoverable and prevents callers from inferring success from result presence. The envelope output cannot replace nested-frame revert bytes. This richer wire contract requires serializer and consumer changes; stable error kinds and exact gas accounting still need agreement.
items.next_step: Agree exact field placement and stable failure kinds. Separate REVERT, exceptional halt and SELFDESTRUCT/no-result cases in fixtures; do not require identical free-text descriptions.
items.rationale: Consumers need the raw revert data and failure identity without parsing implementation-specific English or mistaking a failure for success.
items.recommendation: Always mark a failed CALL/CREATE with error and an explicit result. Preserve that frame’s REVERT return bytes and measured gasUsed when available; use null when no result data applies. The error field determines failure even when result contains data. Never manufacture a successful creation result for a failed CREATE. Define a small stable set of failure kinds; human-readable explanations or decoded revertReason may be optional.
items.title: Failed frame results and error labels

background: Parity's [CreateResult type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L432-L450) has `gasUsed`, `code` and `address`; its [serializer test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L748-L769) expects those exact keys. The [executive tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L112-L125) fills `code` from the completed creation's deployed bytes; the action's `init` records constructor input. The [VM trace type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L109-L124) separately describes executing code.

Parity later [distinguished CREATE from CREATE2](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/87e108058125098ec404951393a054f08aebef7a) and [restored backward-compatible encoding](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/dcc6307f8a5f6037db6c99989d684985be9b8826). That history concerns creation-method metadata, not a change from `code` to `output`. The pinned [Besu flat-trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L330-L365) handles call output and creation code in adjacent branches, making the linked mixed-creation case important for checking where the published result gets its field name.

The zero-fee [constructor](../cases/initial/call-constructor.md) and [environment](../cases/coverage/model-environment-free.md) requests are H15 fee-validation probes. A fee-cap rejection has no creation result to assess, so H10 requires their priced counterparts instead. If a zero-fee request executes, the general creation-result assertion still checks its fields.
items.next_step: Specify creationMethod if it is required; retain the successful mixed-creation probe and investigate historical-method metadata separately.
items.rationale: Creation has two different bytecodes—initcode and deployed code—and their field meanings should remain distinct.
items.recommendation: Use result.address, result.code and result.gasUsed for successful creation. result.code is deployed runtime bytecode, including "0x" for an empty deployment. Use result.output for CALL results; vmTrace.code for executing initcode.
items.title: Creation result field names

background: The [OpenEthereum trace guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_call) describes the requested trace types as an array containing one or more of `vmTrace`, `trace` and `stateDiff`. The [Parity RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L44-L58), however, used a plain vector; its [option mapping and call execution](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L36-L42) have no nonempty guard. With an empty vector all detail tracers are off, while the call still executes and yields its output. This is observed source behavior, not a documented promise.

The linked Nethermind case reaches an internal collection-reduction exception for an empty selection. That is independently a reporting bug. The proposed contract chooses to accept [] because output-only execution is useful and follows the same envelope rules as other selections; it intentionally clarifies the guide’s narrower “one or more” wording. A deliberate -32602 would be well formed but would still differ from this proposed selection policy.
items.next_step: A focused Nethermind fix and regression fixture can proceed independently of the broader API design.
items.rationale: An empty list of auxiliary views is a useful request for execution output alone. Its validity should not depend on whether detail tracers are enabled; fee-validation differences in the captured calls do not establish identical cross-client behavior.
items.recommendation: Accept an empty selection, execute the call and return its output with empty/unrequested components. Never leak a collection-reduction exception.
items.title: Empty trace-type selection

background: The [OpenEthereum guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_rawtransaction) documents only raw bytes and trace types. Parity's [RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L55-L61) and [implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L169), however, accepted an optional third `BlockNumber`, defaulted omission to latest, and used the selected state and header. Explicit pending was rejected. The original published examples and source therefore disagree about whether the third argument was part of the public contract.

The pinned [Reth implementation](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L120-L141) likewise takes an optional block ID and selects its EVM environment; [Erigon](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L1656), [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L141) and the Geth draft fork expose two parameters in the pinned source. Accepted third-argument syntax still requires an observable state-selection test, as the existing decision says.

The third selector is an inherited optional capability omitted from the old guide, not a newly invented Reth feature. The portable two-argument baseline reflects current client coverage while leaving that capability available. Adoption of a shared selector contract requires state-sensitive probes, not just accepted syntax. A historical selector means that block’s post-state; it is not necessarily the selected transaction’s pre-state, so it does not by itself make an already-mined signed transaction valid under H13.
items.next_step: Decide the extension contract with client teams. Keep extension requests and their results outside baseline assessment; preserve complete-response checks independently.
items.rationale: The baseline should be usable on all four today without silently changing which state is traced.
items.recommendation: Standardize the two-argument baseline with latest state. Observe an explicitly supplied third block selector as an extension, without marking its acceptance or rejection as baseline conformance. An accepted request alone does not prove that the selected state was used. Agree extension semantics and unsupported-argument errors separately.
items.title: Raw-transaction block argument

background: [Erigon supports strict execution validation](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890#issuecomment-5784143408), including balance and EIP-3607 sender-code checks. Error-code mapping and compatibility migration require client agreement.

Erigon reports that OpenEthereum skipped nonce checks and could supplement sender balance. Strict validation therefore changes legacy diagnostic behavior. A transaction pool can retain a future-nonce transaction that cannot execute next against the selected state. Block selectors conventionally refer to post-state; use transaction replay to obtain a mined transaction’s actual pre-transaction state.

The raw-validation corpus uses independently verified Prague state, funded controls and observable storage/output markers. It covers both nonce directions, chain identity, value and upfront-gas affordability, intrinsic gas, base fee and sender code, with valid EIP-7702 delegation and execution-OOG controls.

Erigon and Nethermind execute low- and high-nonce CREATE probes at the address derived from the state nonce. Constructor ADDRESS bytes, the returned address and created code in stateDiff agree. This establishes execution semantics without implying mutation of the signed bytes. Besu’s empty success-shaped results and Nethermind’s malformed responses are distinct from demonstrated execution. See the [H13 validation study](../../docs/h13-validation.md) for results and reproduction.

Parity's [raw RPC path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L170) used the same `client.call` as unsigned simulation. Its [virtual-call helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1206-L1233) explicitly disables nonce checking, while [`transact_virtual`](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L819-L833) supplies missing sender balance. The source comment identifies extra-block executions for consensus contracts and RPCs as the purpose of that virtual path. Thus permissiveness was a deliberate shared simulation mechanism in Parity; it is not evidence that modern clients silently rewrote signed bytes.

**Recommendation risk:** strict selected-state rejection gives a truthful execution-validity result but removes Parity's historical hypothetical-inspection behavior for future-nonce or underfunded signed transactions. The [Erigon review comment](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890#issuecomment-5784143408) supports strict execution; it does not by itself settle migration for callers relying on virtual simulation. Keep that compatibility question visible even though the validation direction is converged.
items.next_step: Agree the execution-validity requirements, the proposed -32003 error code and a migration path for permissive diagnostic workflows. Keep H12 block-selection semantics separate.
items.rationale: A signed trace should describe those bytes executing against the selected state. Skipping nonce validation can change CREATE addresses and nonce-dependent behavior; overriding nonce or balance instead invents a different pre-state. Strict validation intentionally tightens historical permissive simulation and can reject queued or already-mined transactions at latest state. Client acceptance alone does not establish a deliberate nonce policy, and malformed error JSON does not prove validation was skipped.
items.recommendation: Validate trace_rawTransaction for execution against the selected state and fork: signature, chain identity, nonce equality (both low and high), balance for value and upfront gas, intrinsic gas, fees and sender-code restrictions with the EIP-7702 delegation exception. Do not change signed fields, override the sender nonce or supplement its balance. This is not pool admission: exclude local replacement, already-known and minimum-tip policies. Propose -32003 (Transaction rejected) for a decodable transaction that fails validation; malformed encoding or parameters use -32602. Valid execution that REVERTs or halts still returns a trace.
items.title: Signed transaction execution validity

background: Parity's [RPC error helpers](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/errors.rs#L145-L178) distinguished invalid parameters from execution errors. The [raw trace handler](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L170) mapped invalid RLP through InvalidParams, while its [transaction-error helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/errors.rs#L466-L481) used a separate server code for transaction errors. [EIP-1474's error table](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#error-codes) later named `-32602` Invalid params and `-32003` Transaction rejected; aligning categories is better grounded than matching historical message text or Parity's private numeric transaction code.

Parity's [trace filter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L27-L46) and [call request](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/call_request.rs#L20-L42) rejected unknown fields. The draft deliberately accepts extra call-object fields for interoperability with shared transaction objects, while keeping filters closed. Known fields must still be validated and conflicting fee fields rejected. Ignoring extras cannot establish extension support and can hide typos; clients must declare supported extensions and callers must not infer support from success. H02 separately retains integer output paths and hex request indices.
items.next_step: Specify accepted types, bounds and unknown-field handling, then align parameter validation; do not conflate validation with EVM errors.
items.rationale: Callers should distinguish a malformed request from a valid request that cannot execute, without text matching.
items.recommendation: Use -32602 for malformed encodings, wrong types and unsupported argument shapes. Use a documented execution/validation error for a well-formed but invalid transaction. Keep messages implementation-specific; omit internal stack traces.
items.title: Invalid-parameter error codes

background: Parity's [call-request adapter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/fake_sign.rs#L24-L37) defaulted an unsigned call's `gasPrice` to zero and fake-signed it for the same [virtual execution path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1206-L1233) used by `trace_call` and `trace_callMany`. That path disabled nonce checks and used the requested block's header; it treated simulations as extra-block execution rather than pool admission. This explains the zero-fee precedent, but Parity predates `BASEFEE`. That is not precedent for preserving every environmental field: Parity's [call executors](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1490-L1538) also replaced the gas limit with U256::max_value(). Preserving the selected block environment is an explicit modern contract choice.

[EIP-1559](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1559#specification) makes the block base fee a separate environmental value and defines `GASPRICE` from the effective transaction price. The H15 probes show why a client should not make a zero-fee simulation succeed by silently changing the selected block's BASEFEE. pre-1559 Parity behavior cannot settle the modern relationship among zero-fee unsigned calls, typed fee fields, `GASPRICE` and simulated balance changes. The draft needs those observable rules, especially for `trace_callMany`, to make the proposed behavior precise; history does not decide these modern rules.

Reth's [unsigned-call environment](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/helpers/call.rs#L876-L906) disables base-fee validation and fee charging, then sets the EVM block base fee to zero when the call's gas price is zero. Both [trace_call](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L98-L109) and [trace_callMany](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L149-L169) use this call setup. In the pinned [zero-fee](../cases/coverage/model-environment-free.md) probe, the tested release and development builds return GASPRICE 0 and BASEFEE 0 although the selected block's base fee is 765625000 wei. In the [priced](../cases/coverage/model-environment.md) probe, they return the supplied GASPRICE of 2 gwei and the original BASEFEE, but stateDiff shows no gas-fee debit. These are implementation observations, not client-team agreement; the callMany fixture confirms zero-fee execution but does not independently probe its BASEFEE opcode value.
items.next_step: Agree the fee-free simulation rule, then fix the block-environment discrepancy. The source contract confirms BASEFEE is returned as word 3; this is more than an error-message difference.
items.rationale: Relaxing transaction admission for a hypothetical call should not silently rewrite the block the caller selected.
items.recommendation: Allow explicit zero-fee unsigned simulations without changing the selected block’s BASEFEE or other block fields. With nonzero supplied fees, use those fees consistently in opcode context and simulated accounting. Apply the same policy to trace_call and trace_callMany; keep strict signed validation separate.
items.title: Unsigned simulation fees and block environment

background: Parity's [multi-call executor](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1518-L1538) applies each call to one mutable state in order. Its [virtual-call helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1218-L1237) clones state immediately before a requested state diff, so each result describes that call relative to the preceding call's post-state. The [OpenEthereum multi-call guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_callmany) describes the same dependent-call purpose. This is stronger historical grounding than treating each result as an independent `trace_call` from the original block.

Parity's pre-1559 [transaction finalizer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L1160-L1175) refunded the sender and credited the block author with fees. [EIP-1559](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1559#specification) later split the effective gas price into a burned base fee and a beneficiary tip. Thus replay and signed raw traces should reflect the fork-correct actual state transition, while unsigned calls need the separate H15 fee policy. The pinned client state-diff sources and linked cases test the modern result; Parity alone cannot establish post-1559 accounting.
items.next_step: Resolve fee and environment rules while preserving storage carry-over, reverted EVM-write rollback and simulation isolation. Add warm-access reset, refunds and blob-fee accounting probes; current output/storage/nonce cases do not establish complete fee accounting.
items.rationale: A state diff should be internally coherent and reconstructible; an ordered multi-call simulation should have one predictable state timeline.
items.recommendation: For signed/raw and mined replay, report the complete actual transition: sender pays value plus gas, fee recipient gets the tip, base fee is burned. For unsigned calls use H15’s documented policy consistently. Each callMany result should describe its own transition from the preceding call’s post-state, not a cumulative diff from the original state. Reverted EVM writes roll back, while fork-defined transaction-level nonce and fee effects survive.
items.title: Fee accounting and sequential state diffs

background: Parity's [account diff algorithm](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L134) compares optional account existence before comparing fields: absent-to-present marks balance, nonce, code and present storage as Born; present-to-absent marks them Died; present-to-present uses Same or Changed. Its [RPC serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L160-L207) encodes those variants as `+`, `-`, `=` and `*`. The [original create/delete test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/state.rs#L88-L114) explicitly expects a newly created account's zero nonce and empty code to be `+`.

This history explains why `+` is an existence marker, not shorthand for a nonzero or nonempty value. A pre-existing empty-code account is therefore a changed or unchanged account, not a birth. The linked modern stateDiff cases should be checked against pre-state existence as well as byte values; output shape alone cannot establish whether a client classified the account correctly.
items.next_step: Review account-creation markers separately from the prefunded-empty-account check. Agree the existence model across balance, code, nonce and storage deltas.
items.rationale: Absent and existing-but-empty are different states; consumers should be able to reconstruct the change without guessing.
items.recommendation: Make account existence explicit: + for fields of a newly created account (including empty code and nonce zero), - for deletion, * for a changed existing value, = for unchanged existing fields. If an address already existed with empty code, do not mark it as newly created. Compare existence at the execution endpoints; transient creation and destruction with an account absent at both endpoints does not produce an account diff.
items.title: New-account stateDiff encoding

background: Parity's [state-diff algorithm](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L136) compares account code in the pre- and post-state independently of trace actions. That predates EIP-7702 but supplies the right historical meaning of `stateDiff.code`: changed existing code uses `*`, new-account code uses `+`, and deletion uses `-`. The pinned [Reth state-diff path](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs) and linked authorization cases show an implementation can miss code written during transaction preprocessing even when later EVM execution is traced.

[EIP-7702](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702#behavior) writes a delegation indicator or clears code while processing authorizations before the execution portion. It explicitly preserves processed authorizations even if the later execution reverts. The EIP's rationale explains why delegation was made persistent. A complete transaction state diff therefore has to include the authorization-side code change despite a failed call frame.

EIP-7702 permits multiple valid tuples from one authority, with the last valid code write winning. stateDiff reports their net effect, not each intermediate write. Authorization processing also skips certain invalid tuples without rejecting an otherwise valid outer transaction; H13’s execution-validity rule must follow those fork-defined distinctions. Event-level authorization history would require a separate output contract.
items.next_step: Fix net account code-change reporting and add multiple-authorizations probes, including a final code value equal to the pre-state. Distinguish invalid outer transactions from authorization tuples skipped under EIP-7702.
items.rationale: stateDiff must include code that changed, even if the account already existed.
items.recommendation: Report net pre/post delegation-code changes, including set, replace and clear, independently of account-creation flags. Preserve authorization effects when later execution reverts. Multiple accepted authorizations that restore the original code produce no net code change, although nonce changes may remain.
items.title: EIP-7702 code changes in stateDiff

background: Parity's [VM tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L277-L296) stores the `code` bytes passed when an execution subtrace begins, and the [executor](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L953-L966) passes the chosen action's code, not a later address lookup. This explains the original `vmTrace.code` field as executing bytecode. For CREATE that is initcode, while H10's `result.code` is deployed runtime code.

[EIP-7702](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702#delegation-indicator) adds delegation-code resolution after Parity's era: execution follows one indicated target and stops after that first hop, while external code-reading opcodes inspect the indicator itself. The trace therefore needs the resolved executed bytes in a delegated frame, not the authority's 23-byte indicator or a stale pre-state lookup. The pinned [Reth trace builder](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs) and [inspector dependency](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/blob/453c67d7ccdf51327c9e7687ac6ba0b8651e7f87/src/tracing/builder/parity.rs) are the relevant modern path for the linked missing-initcode case.
items.next_step: Fix bytecode population separately from the already-retested instruction deltas. Add EIP-7702 one-hop controls: a delegation target that itself delegates must not be followed recursively, and delegation to a precompile executes empty code rather than the native precompile.
items.rationale: The operations must be decodable against the bytes in their own frame.
items.recommendation: Record the bytecode actually executed in each frame: initcode for creation, resolved implementation code for delegation, and the relevant code source for delegatecall/callcode. Do not populate it from an address-only pre-state lookup after tracing.
items.title: vmTrace executing bytecode

background: Parity's [interpreter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L348-L405) calls the VM tracer before an opcode with its cost and reported memory region, then after the opcode with the current remaining gas, pushed stack words and memory. The [VM tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L241-L274) stores that after-step gas in the value serialized as `ex.used` and extracts that post-step memory slice. Its internal field is named `gas_used`, but the passed value is remaining gas; the recommendation follows the execution path rather than the misleading name.

[EIP-5656](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5656#semantics) introduced MCOPY after Parity's codebase and defines it as an actual destination-memory write, including overlapping copies. The pinned [Besu VM generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/vm/VmTraceGenerator.java) and [Erigon VM tracer](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L545) should classify MCOPY's destination and capture its post-operation bytes. The original hook design does not determine the exact gas boundary for trapped nested calls, which remains a separate fixture question.

Parity's [memory-region calculation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L472-L493) included MLOAD and the entire requested CALL output window. Those were post-step snapshots, not exclusively writes. The draft deliberately narrows mem to bytes actually written: memory expansion is distinct from a byte write, and a short return must not claim the untouched tail of the requested output window. This refinement needs explicit fixtures rather than an appeal to Parity compatibility.
items.next_step: Retain the fixed regressions. Add MLOAD with and without expansion, short CALL output over a nonzero tail, empty return data, zero-length/OOG copies, and nested warm-access/stipend/refund probes. Separate actual writes from memory expansion and snapshots.
items.rationale: Same-step effects let consumers follow execution without shifting writes between opcodes. Memory-write deltas alone do not encode allocated memory size; reconstructing expansion also needs opcode context.
items.recommendation: Define ex.used as post-operation gas remaining, and mem/store/push as effects of that same operation. Use null for no memory write, with actual offset and bytes for a write. Specify call/return gas boundaries using dedicated nested-call fixtures before choosing detailed gas formulas.
items.title: vmTrace step timing and deltas

background: Parity's [VM operation type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L43-L124) serializes pushed stack items as `U256` quantities, but code and memory deltas as byte data. Its original operation record has `pc`, `cost`, `ex` and `sub`; it does not require mnemonic `op` or sequence `idx` fields. [EIP-1474's encoding rules](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#value-encoding) distinguish minimal `Quantity` values such as `0x0` from even-length `Data` bytes such as `0x00`, which explains the recommendation's different encodings.

The pinned [Nethermind VM serializer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Blockchain/Tracing/ParityStyle/ParityVmOperationTraceConverter.cs#L40-L67) serializes its stored `Push` items directly; the linked cases show padded words. Adding `op` or `idx` can help tools display a trace, but the original Parity record did not need them to reproduce execution. Their presence should therefore be checked for consistency without making older traces invalid.
items.next_step: Agree schema types and extension policy. A diagnostic comparison may show a separate typed-semantic projection, but must retain the exact wire differences.
items.rationale: Numeric values and byte arrays have different formatting needs; optional convenience labels should not determine whether a trace can be consumed.
items.recommendation: Encode stack words as minimal hex quantities (zero is 0x0), memory/code as even-length byte strings. Make op/idx optional metadata; require consumers to accept their absence and validate consistency when present. Keep required execution fields independent of these annotations. Keep pc, cost, used and traceAddress as JSON integers. Validate idx only against an explicitly defined numbering convention.
items.title: vmTrace numeric and optional metadata encoding

background: Parity's [executive tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L106) records a root precompile as a call frame and writes the actual bytes passed to `done_trace_call` into that frame's `result.output`. The separate [execution envelope](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L646) carries `output` from the completed execution even when no VM bytecode operations exist. Thus the two output locations refer to the same return bytes for a successful root call; the absence of EVM code is not a reason to empty either one.

The pinned [Besu flat-trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L70-L125) special-cases a precompiled gas cost while constructing the root frame. The linked identity-precompile case is a direct discriminator: an execution envelope with correct return bytes does not prove the corresponding frame's result was populated. H29 separately decides which nested precompile frames exist.
items.next_step: A focused Besu reporting fix and regression fixture can proceed without waiting on broad API policy.
items.rationale: Two views of the same successful call should not disagree about its return value.
items.recommendation: Report actual return bytes in each successful call-frame result, including precompiles with no EVM bytecode. The execution envelope output must equal the successful root call’s output; nested calls can return different bytes.
items.title: Precompile return bytes

background: Parity's [original address matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L82-L110) assigns sender/recipient equivalents per action: CREATE uses the creator and successful result address, SELFDESTRUCT uses the destroyed account and refund address, and PoW reward uses its author as the recipient. This mapping is part of the indexed filter implementation, not a reinterpretation of a generic `to` field. The pinned Besu CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT cases test that the same records visible in `trace_block` can be found by their relevant addresses.

[Parity issue #9822](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/issues/9822) reported that `trace_filter` dropped a failed contract creation visible by transaction/block tracing; [the fix](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/1ac1224cd3f983d66d650e78428d274350c84a30) addressed that historical edge. a failed CREATE has no successful `result.address`. Parity's matcher still allows a creator-only query to find it but cannot satisfy a nonempty recipient filter. The proposed mapping preserves that distinction instead of assigning a successful destination to a failed creation.
items.next_step: Agree the action mapping and add the discriminating filter fixtures.
items.rationale: Address-based history should not silently omit a transfer or creation because its action uses different field names.
items.recommendation: Define from/to equivalents per action: creator/successfully created address for CREATE, destroyed account/refund beneficiary for SELFDESTRUCT, and recipient only for rewards. A failed CREATE has no successful recipient address: it can match its creator, but not a populated recipient list. Apply H03 composition, so union can retain that creator match. Matching a reverted action does not imply a committed transfer.
items.title: Special-action address matching

background: Parity's [original flat tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L151) pushes a frame index on entry, then writes either its result or its failure to that exact frame when the EVM exits it. Its child count and traceAddress advance independently of the outcome. This is the historical reason to attach an error to a call frame rather than infer it from another frame's opcode stream: an EVM caller can inspect a failed CALL's success bit and then return successfully.

In the pinned [Besu flat trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L549-L565), `hasRevertInSubCall` scans the transaction-wide trace frames for a matching depth, without first delimiting the current call's subtree. It is used when assigning the root and nested frame errors. That explains why the sibling fixtures can report a handled revert on the wrong frame; the observed trace result remains the regression oracle for this diagnosis.
items.next_step: Prepare a focused Besu regression and fix without waiting for broad schema policy.
items.rationale: A successful caller can handle a failed subcall and continue; frame results must preserve that distinction.
items.recommendation: Attach error and result data to the actual call frame. A sibling failure must not change another frame's status. A child’s local success remains success even if a later ancestor revert rolls back its state changes; frame outcome and committed stateDiff answer different questions.
items.title: Sibling failure isolation

background: Parity's [original `trace_rawTransaction` implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L168) parses RLP, validates the signed transaction and resolves the state/header before returning a `Result<TraceResults>`; each failure maps to an RPC error instead of a partial trace object. The later [Ethereum RPC error specification](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474) likewise describes an `error` member on the response object, so this decision concerns response integrity independently of which signed transactions a client accepts.

The pinned [Nethermind trace module](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L141-L177) validates RLP before tracing but, when streaming is enabled, `BuildStreamingSingleResult` returns a lazy streaming result whose execution runs while the JSON writer is active. This makes a late admission or execution failure a different problem from malformed RLP. prevalidating the request alone cannot ensure a complete JSON-RPC error if a deferred trace fails after result bytes have been sent; buffering or an error-safe streaming boundary is needed for that guarantee. An explicit transport abort is an incomplete request, not a successful trace or a complete JSON-RPC error; it cannot count as passing the semantic assessment.
items.next_step: Retain raw malformed-response evidence. Test both pre-commit JSON-RPC errors and post-commit failures through the actual transport, including later callMany validation and cancellation; distinguish explicit transport aborts from malformed completed responses.
items.rationale: Clients must be able to parse failures and associate them with a request, regardless of the chosen signed-transaction admission policy.
items.recommendation: Before committing result bytes, report validation or execution setup failures as one complete JSON-RPC error. Buffer when necessary to guarantee a replaceable response. After output has been committed, a later failure must explicitly abort the transport rather than append a second envelope or finish a partial result as success. Request parsing alone is not full validation; later callMany admission can depend on earlier calls.
items.title: Well-formed errors for rejected raw transactions

background: Parity's [original account diff](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L140) distinguishes a present account becoming absent (`Died` for balance, nonce, code and each prior storage slot supplied to that helper) from an account that remains present with changed values. Its [transaction finalizer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L1132-L1181) actually removed SELFDESTRUCT accounts at the end of execution under those pre-Cancun rules. The deletion markers therefore describe account existence, not merely a zeroed balance.

[EIP-6780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6780) deliberately changed that premise: SELFDESTRUCT normally transfers the balance without deleting a pre-existing account's code or storage, preserving deletion only for a contract created in the same transaction. This explains why the selected block's fork rules determine the stateDiff, and why the Nethermind/Reth pre-Cancun missing code and nonce markers are meaningful. `stateDiff` compares the before and after account snapshots. A contract created and destroyed within the same transaction can leave no account at either endpoint, so even genuine transient deletion need not produce a `Died` entry; an execution trace is needed to see that event. A prefunded address, however, existed before creation; deletion at that address can require a net deletion entry.

The helper is not evidence that historical traces enumerated every old slot: [Account::to_pod](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/account-state/src/account.rs#L142-L157) exposes storage_changes, while [state diff construction](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/account-state/src/state.rs#L868-L926) builds partial account snapshots. Exhaustive storage enumeration has a different cost from reporting account deletion and must be specified explicitly.
items.next_step: Retain deletion-marker regressions. Add untouched nonzero storage and same-transaction creation/destruction at both absent and prefunded addresses. The current empty-storage case does not establish complete slot enumeration.
items.rationale: Deletion and a zero balance with retained code are observably different states. Apply the rules of the selected block.
items.recommendation: Compare account existence before and after the execution. For present-to-absent accounts, use deletion markers for balance, nonce and code; account deletion implies clearing all storage. The policy for enumerating untouched prior storage slots still needs agreement. After EIP-6780 a pre-existing contract normally survives SELFDESTRUCT, so do not report code deletion. An account absent at both endpoints has no net account diff, even if created and destroyed during execution.
items.title: Account deletion across Cancun

background: Parity's [original trace database filter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L349-L365) searched indexed trace blooms over the requested range, loaded each stored block's traces, and filtered those records. The trace namespace thus established per-block result consistency without requiring a range request to execute blocks again. This matters across forks because each stored trace was produced with the rules in force when its block was imported.

The pinned [Besu range pipeline](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceFilter.java#L142-L202) obtains one `protocolSpec` and transaction processor from its first block header, then feeds a list of blocks to the pipeline. That is a plausible cause of the reproduced difference between a cross-fork filter and the same individual block traces; the fixture comparison, rather than code inspection alone, establishes the defect. The requirement is output equivalence and fork-correct provenance, not a mandate to re-execute indexed traces.
items.next_step: The repeated fixtures are ready for a focused processor-context investigation and regression.
items.rationale: The same block must not trace differently depending on the other blocks included in a query.
items.recommendation: Return records produced with each block’s own fork rules and state, whether retrieved from an index or replayed. Filtering and pagination over the ordered range must agree with the corresponding per-block records. Do not reuse one block’s execution rules across a fork boundary.
items.title: Filter execution across fork boundaries

background: Parity's [original replay path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1639-L1667) obtained `state_at_beginning(block)` from the parent block's post-state, then applied the selected block's transactions in order with its own environment. That is the lineage for distinguishing replay's pre-block starting state from the post-state used by a historical simulated call. Parity predates the current beacon-root and block-hash system writes, so its transaction-only loop is not a complete modern replay recipe.

[EIP-4788](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788) and [EIP-2935](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2935) perform their system updates at the start of the selected block, before transactions. Consequently, block N's post-state includes those writes and block N+1's does not belong in a query at N. Erigon [PR #24056](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/24056), merged on 2026-09-18 as [66571d04390](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/commit/66571d043907723f190fbe1f882008c27008fa29), identified a history reader opened one transaction index too late: Min(N+1)+1 included the next block's system call. It changes the historical trace_call, debug_traceCall and default-index debug_traceCallMany readers from txnIndex 0 to -1 and adds TestTraceCallExcludesNextBlockSystemCall. The maintainer explicitly retained 0 for trace_callMany because that method selects the parent block. The captured v3.6.1 release predates the fix; development c25b8e47 contains it and passes the H28 checks.
items.kind: Historical-state discrepancy fixed on Erigon main
items.next_step: Verify release uptake of Erigon #24056. All captured native development builds match H28; unrelated H09 schema failures still block the stricter harmonization milestone. Extend coverage to transaction ordering and additional system operations.
items.rationale: A future system write must not appear in an earlier block's state. This is an execution-context issue, not a cosmetic trace encoding choice.
items.recommendation: Historical state at block N should include that block's changes, including system operations, but none from N+1. Replay should start from the appropriate parent state and apply each system transition once.
items.title: Historical state at system-operation boundaries

background: Parity's [original ExecutiveTracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L108) explicitly skipped only a non-root built-in call whose `ActionParams.value.value()` was zero. It incremented the parent's subtrace count and path only for retained frames; its success and failure callbacks both cleared the skip flag for an omitted built-in. That is the trace namespace's historical frame policy, rather than a consequence of whether the precompile did useful computation or succeeded.

The old [ActionValue definition](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/vm/src/action_params.rs#L29-L62) makes `value()` return either a transferred or an apparent value. A DELEGATECALL can therefore retain a frame because it inherits a nonzero apparent value even though it moves no funds. The pinned [Besu generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L280-L313) skips precompile calls during frame construction; the crossed outer/child value fixtures isolate the incompatibility. This inherited-value exception is a historical compatibility rule, not a value-transfer assertion.
items.next_step: Review the inherited DELEGATECALL exception as a compatibility choice and extend to more precompiles/forks. The precompile-values corpus separates outer and child values, pre-funds zero-value creations with a preceding simulated transfer, and returns the call success bit. Parent error propagation remains a separate H24 issue.
items.rationale: The retained inherited-value exception is a compatibility choice, not a statement that DELEGATECALL transfers funds. Crossed-value CALL/CALLCODE fixtures confirm that Erigon, Reth and Nethermind use the explicit child value rather than the outer value. Besu still omits the nonzero-value child. The independent Geth draft implementation also matches these checks; it is not an independent vote for the policy.
items.recommendation: Retain root precompile calls. Omit nested precompile frames with zero value; retain those with nonzero transferred or inherited value, whether successful or failed. Number traceAddress and subtraces over the emitted tree. Keep caller VM return-memory effects even when a child frame is omitted.
items.title: Precompile call-frame inclusion

background: The pinned draft initially described an earliest-to-latest default. In the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md), both pinned Besu and Nethermind builds start at head 48; Erigon and Reth start at block 1, as does the experimental Geth draft fork. An explicit head-only query succeeds on all builds. These observations establish the split, not client-team agreement on a standard.

Parity’s [original filter conversion](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L44-L68) explicitly used `Latest` for both omitted bounds; its pending fallback and address defaults are separate choices. Pinned [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L278-L296) preserves that default. The live case with only `toBlock: 2` exposes the difference more clearly than an empty object: a latest implicit start at head 48 cannot reach block 2. Besu reports `-32602`, Nethermind `-32000`; the proposal requires a range error but leaves its code for review.

Parity could serve historical queries from an [indexed trace database](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L349-L365), whereas modern clients may replay range blocks. A [Reth operator report](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/24473) documents heavy replay load from much smaller explicit ranges. The earlier earliest-to-latest recommendation made an omitted lower bound convenient for historical search, but could turn an ordinary query into an unbounded replay. `count` limits returned records, not scan or replay work.

The historical direction is especially clear in Parity’s log filter: its [April 2016 change](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/fd2d55934b5285d213661014e064d7aa64ca497b) explicitly replaced an `earliest` default with `latest`, before the [May 2016 trace namespace introduction](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/7c2adc41375d021e40c9c1e6456aeb6a8e7623a9) gave `trace_filter` latest/latest defaults from the start. Today [Ethereum.org documents](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/#eth-getlogs) `eth_getLogs` fromBlock and toBlock as latest by default, and pinned [Geth](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/572bd3696587d4f9599d577c3211c23985f7e4d1/eth/filters/api.go#L466-L482) and [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-types/src/logs_utils.rs#L156-L177) implement that choice. The current [execution-apis filter schema](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/5bcdc34a477b10af278c079525374e6a4046f291/src/schemas/filter.yaml#L13-L24) permits both fields to be omitted but does not itself declare their defaults, so the trace profile makes its choice explicit.

**Compatibility cost:** callers relying on implicit historical search in Erigon, Reth or the Geth draft fork must supply `fromBlock`. On pinned [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L352-L393), an omitted start currently resolves to block 0; a pruned node rejects that history and even an archive node rejects a range above its [default 100-block limit](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc-server-types/src/constants.rs#L17-L20). Latest/latest avoids that ordinary-request failure. Explicit history must still preserve the requested start and return a pruned-history or resource-limit error if it cannot be served; it must not silently shift to the retention boundary or truncate success.
items.next_step: Confirm latest/latest and reversed-range error semantics with client teams; align Erigon, Reth and the experimental Geth draft fork. Agree explicit range limits and a common error code for reversed ranges; add a pruned-node explicit-history case. count limits returned records, not execution work.
items.rationale: This preserves Parity/OpenEthereum’s original trace_filter default and matches the documented eth_getLogs convention. A plain filter targets only the current head, so a small count does not leave a chain-wide range implicit or request history that may be pruned or exceed a range cap. Historical callers must name fromBlock; explicit bounds retain their meaning. On the frozen fixture, head is 48, so the omitted-bounds query matches an explicit 48-to-48 query, while toBlock 2 alone is reversed.
items.recommendation: Default omitted fromBlock and toBlock to latest, resolving both against the same canonical head at request start. An explicit toBlock older than an omitted fromBlock is a reversed range and must return a range error. Respect explicit endpoints, then filter and paginate the ordered range. Return 4444 when explicitly requested history is unavailable; report resource limits explicitly rather than silently narrowing the range or returning incomplete success.
items.title: Omitted trace_filter range bounds

background: All tested builds return NUMBER 48 for trace_callMany at explicit latest and for trace_call with omitted or explicit latest. With trace_callMany's block omitted, Besu rejects the argument count, Erigon and Nethermind return 48, and Reth returns 49. The pinned schema marks the block argument optional; see the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md).

Parity's [original `trace_callMany` implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L119-L145) accepts an optional block parameter and uses the same `unwrap_or_default()` as `trace_call`; [BlockNumber's default](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/block_number.rs#L43-L47) is `Latest`. Both methods resolve a state and header for that selected block. Thus the proposed default follows the original namespace's API contract and the explicit-latest cross-client control, while Besu's argument-count failure is a request-shape incompatibility.

Pinned [Reth code](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L146-L190) deliberately defaults omitted `trace_callMany` to `BlockId::pending()` and describes sequential calls atop a pending block; its observed NUMBER 49 is consistent with a next-block environment. Choosing latest intentionally changes that established Reth default when pending differs from latest. The sequential application of calls can still work under either selector, so the issue is the omitted selector's compatibility and environment, not whether callMany is sequential.
items.next_step: Confirm optionality and the latest default with client teams; document the migration for Besu callers that currently must pass a block and Reth callers that rely on an omitted block selecting pending.
items.rationale: The same unsigned simulation should not silently change its block environment when batched. The frozen NUMBER constructor returns 48 at latest and 49 in Reth's pending environment, making the difference observable without mempool transactions.
items.recommendation: Make the trace_callMany block argument optional and default it to latest, matching trace_call. An explicit block selector must override that default; explicit pending is handled under H32.
items.title: Omitted trace_callMany block

background: The pinned filter schema lists earliest, finalized, safe, latest and pending, while the draft profile leaves pending-state behavior and pending localization open. In the live capture, Erigon and Nethermind resolve safe filter bounds; Besu returns -32603 and Reth -32602. Erigon development rejects pending with -32000 while its release resolves it to mined block 48. See the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md).

The explicit earliest-to-block-2 filter is compared with an explicit block-0-to-block-2 control. Nethermind returns [] for both because of its separately tracked history issue; that equivalence is evidence about tag parsing, not complete trace retrieval. Finalized and unavailable safe/finalized were not exercised.

Parity's original pending behavior was method-specific: the [filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L44-L68) warned and silently substituted `latest`; [`trace_block`](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L67-L78) returned `null`; simulations and replay with a pending block argument rejected it as invalid parameters. These choices predate safe/finalized selectors and did not define a shared pending state or a way to localize mined and pending trace records consistently. That history supports specifying pending per method rather than inheriting one global tag behavior.

**Recommendation risk:** explicitly rejecting pending collection requests until a contract is agreed changes Parity's historical filter fallback and `trace_block` null response. That is probably clearer to callers, but it should be recorded as a compatibility decision. The live safe-tag checks establish parsing only on available endpoints; they do not yet prove semantics for an unavailable safe/finalized head, so the recommendation's word `resolvable` matters.
items.next_step: Agree per-method tag support and pending semantics, then add finalized/unavailable-finality and pending-transaction fixtures. Track Nethermind's genesis-range omission through its existing fix rather than treating it as a tag-default result.
items.rationale: A caller must be able to tell whether a tag was rejected, resolved to a mined block, or evaluated in a pending environment. In the frozen fixture, safe resolves to head 48, while Reth's pending call environment exposes NUMBER 49. These observations do not establish mempool transaction inclusion.
items.recommendation: Accept resolvable earliest, latest, safe and finalized selectors where the trace method takes a block or range endpoint. Specify pending separately for collection queries and simulations: whether it is supported, which state and next-block environment it uses, and how pending trace records are localized. Until that contract is agreed, report unsupported pending explicitly; a valid tag must not produce an internal error. Resolve selectors against one consistent chain view for the request.
